title: Pineapple and coconut cake
subtitle: a moist coconut sponge layered with pineapple curd and coconut buttercream
excerpt: Pineapple and coconut cake is two layers of coconut sponge sandwiched with pineapple curd and a creamy coconut buttercream. The sponge is made with desiccated coconut folded into the batter, giving the crumb a slightly dense, moist texture. The pineapple curd is sharp and intensely fruity against the sweetness of the buttercream.
sourceNotes: Pineapple and coconut as a combination is widespread in Caribbean, South American, and South-East Asian desserts. In British baking, tropical fruit layer cakes became popular through the 1970s and 1980s, influenced by the wider availability of tinned tropical fruits.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pineapple curd can be made 3 days ahead and kept refrigerated. Assemble on the day or the day before; keep refrigerated.

content.text: Pineapple and coconut cake is a coconut sponge layered with sharp pineapple curd and a simple coconut buttercream. The sponge batter has desiccated coconut folded through it, which gives the crumb a moist, slightly dense texture that holds up well to layering. The pineapple curd is made like a fruit curd: fruit juice, butter, eggs, and sugar cooked until thick.

items.prepNote: from a tin or fresh, for curd

content.text: Make the pineapple curd: whisk the pineapple juice, caster sugar, and eggs together in a small saucepan. Add the butter. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, for 8 to 10 minutes until the curd is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Pour into a bowl, press cling film onto the surface, and refrigerate until cold.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Grease and line two 20 cm sandwich tins.

Beat the softened butter and caster sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour, baking powder, desiccated coconut, and coconut milk until just combined. Divide evenly between the prepared tins and smooth the tops.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 15 minutes, then turn out onto a rack to cool completely.
Make the coconut buttercream: beat the softened butter until pale and fluffy. Add the sifted icing sugar in two additions, beating well. Add the coconut cream and beat until smooth.

Spread the cold pineapple curd over one sponge layer. Top with a generous layer of coconut buttercream, then place the second sponge on top. Spread or swirl more buttercream on the top. Press toasted coconut around the edge or over the top if using.

attrs.problem: Pineapple curd stays liquid after cooking
attrs.avoid: Avoid cooking on too high heat too fast; the eggs can curdle rather than thicken evenly.
attrs.fix: Cook over medium-low heat and stir constantly. The curd thickens gradually. Once it coats the back of a spoon and holds a clear line when you draw a finger through it, it is ready. Refrigerating causes it to firm up significantly more.

attrs.problem: Sponge dry and dense rather than moist
attrs.avoid: Avoid over-baking; the desiccated coconut makes the crumb slightly drier than a standard sponge.
attrs.fix: Check at 25 minutes. The sponge is done when a skewer comes out clean and the top springs back to a light touch.
